sanskrit: tvacāpidhāne subhage datparistaraṇe kave | ekām iva vraje gāṃ pari tvā varcasāsicam ||
english: O fair one, with skin as thy covering and teeth as thy bedding, O wise one — as one pours abundance around a single cow in the pen, so have I poured radiance around thee.

sanskrit: agreṇīr iva haṃsānāṃ prapaśyantī puras patham | jihve mā vivyatho mā yathāpūrvaṃ tvaṃ vada ||
english: Like the foremost of geese gazing ahead upon the path before — O tongue, do not tremble, do not falter; speak thou as thou hast spoken before.

sanskrit: varcasvad aham udyāsaṃ brahmarājanyābhyāṃ śudrāya cāryāya ca | yasmai ca kāmayāmahe sarvasmai ca vipaśyate ||
english: Radiant may I rise, before the Brahmin and the Rājanya, before the Śūdra and the Ārya, and before whomsoever we desire, and before every one who sees.

sanskrit: arvāñcau pādau pra hara- -arvācīnaṃ manas tava | arvācīnasya te ataḥ parāṅ manyuṃ ni vartatām ||
english: Step forward with both feet turned hither; let thy mind be turned toward me hither. Let thy wrath, which was turned away from thee who now faces me, turn back.

sanskrit: chāgalāde bhagavo 'rvāg jyote parastamaḥ | ā tvā khalajñakād asmāt punar ā vartayāmasi ||
english: O blessed goat-eating one, there is light here in front, darkness beyond. From this threshing-floor knowledge we turn thee back again hither.

sanskrit: yathā vrīhīn vrīhikhale samākurvanti tūlibhiḥ | evā te viṣṭhitaṃ manaḥ sam ā karomi mām abhi ||
english: As they gather rice together on the rice-threshing floor with flails, so I gather together thy scattered mind toward me.

sanskrit: tvam uttamaṃ surabhiṣāṃ mādhyamaṃ vahator asi | tvayā vadhūr vi jaṅgahe taṃ tvā varcasa ā dade ||
english: Thou art the best of fragrant things, the middlemost of what is carried. By thee the bride exults; that splendour of thine do I take unto myself.

sanskrit: mūrdhnas te mūrdhanyebhyo 'gruvaḥ pativittyāḥ | aukṣaṃ śīrṣata ā dade ||
english: From the crown-born ones of thy crown, O unaged woman who has found her husband — I take the bull's sap from the head.

sanskrit: yaś ca svādmā te aṅgeṣu yaḥ premā hṛdaye ca te | taṃ tvad ā veśayāmahe mayi bhrājāti dīdyat ||
english: That sweetness which is in thy limbs and that love which is in thy heart — that we draw out from thee and cause to shine blazing in me.

sanskrit: vātaraṃhā vājin bhava yujyamāna indrasya yāhi prasave manojavāḥ | yuñjantu tvā maruto daivyāsa ā te tvaṣṭā patsu javaṃ dadhātu ||
english: Be swift as the wind, O steed; being yoked, go at Indra's urging, swift as thought. Let the divine Maruts yoke thee; let Tvaṣṭṛ place swiftness in thy feet.

sanskrit: javas te arvan nihito guhā yaḥ śyene carati yaś ca vāte | tena tvaṃ vājin balavān balena- -ājiñ jaya samane pārayiṣṇuḥ ||
english: That swiftness of thine, O steed, stored in the secret place, which moves in the eagle and which moves in the wind — with that, O steed, strong with strength, win the race, able to carry through to the finish.

sanskrit: āsīyāne 'dhi manasa āsīyāne 'dhi cakṣuṣaḥ | āsīyānasya vātād bhūtvā- -ājiñ jaya samane pārayiṣṇuḥ ||
english: Upon the seated one's mind, upon the seated one's eye — becoming like the wind of the one who is sitting, win the race, able to carry through to the finish.

sanskrit: tanūs te vājin tanvaṃ vahantī vāmam asmabhyaṃ dhātu śarma tubhyam | ahruto maho dharuṇāya devā divyam iva jyotiḥ svar ānamīyāḥ ||
english: Thy body, O steed, bearing thy frame, shall bestow bounty on us, comfort on thee. O unharmed one, the great gods for sustenance would make thee bend down like a heavenly light, like the sun.

sanskrit: indro mā vakṣad akṣataṃ vṛtrahā yo vṛtañjayaḥ | sa me rathaṃ sa sārathiṃ so aśvān sādhu me nayāt ||
english: May Indra, the Vṛtra-slayer who conquers the obstructer, carry me across unharmed. May he well guide for me the chariot, the charioteer, and the horses.

sanskrit: indro mā tena nayatu panthā yo abhayaḥ sugaḥ | dakṣiṇā pārayāti mā mā riṣaṃ samare yudhām ||
english: May Indra lead me by that path which is fearless and easy to travel. May he carry me across to the right; may I not be harmed in the meeting of combatants.

sanskrit: hṛtsuke pari ṇo nama pārigaṃ tanve kṛdhi | yuyuta parṇinaṃ śaram utāparṇaṃ riśād iti ||
english: O heart's delight, bow down around us; make a complete circuit for the body. Ward off the feathered arrow and also the unfeathered one that wounds.

sanskrit: viśve devā idaṃ havir ādityāsaḥ saparyata | asmin yajñe mā vyathiṣy amṛtāya haviṣ kṛtam ||
english: All gods, O Ādityas, honour this oblation. In this sacrifice do not waver; the oblation is made for immortality.

sanskrit: avyasaś ca vyacasaś ca bilaṃ vi ṣyāmi māyayā | tābhyām udbhṛtya vedam atha karmāṇi kṛṇmahe ||
english: Both the narrow and the wide pit I open with my magic power. Drawing forth the sacred knowledge from both of them, then we perform the ritual acts.

sanskrit: yasmāt kośād udabharāma vedaṃ tasminn antar ava dadhma enam | kṛtam iṣṭaṃ brahmaṇo vīryeṇa tena mā devās tapasāvateha ||
english: From the vessel out of which we have drawn the Veda, into that same vessel we place it back again. By the might of the Brahman, with what has been offered and accomplished, may the gods protect me here with fervent power.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaro ajījanad agnir no navyāṃ sumatim | kṣmayā vṛdhāna ojasā ||
english: Vaiśvānara, the universal Agni, has engendered a fresh goodwill for us, growing great with the earth's strength.

sanskrit: sa naḥ pāvaka dīhihy agne vaiśvānara dyumat | jamadagnibhir āhutaḥ ||
english: O purifying one, O Agni Vaiśvānara, shine brilliantly for us, invoked with the Jamadagnins' oblations.

sanskrit: divas pṛṣṭho arocathā agnir vaiśvānaro bṛhan | jyotiṣā bādhate tamaḥ ||
english: The great Agni Vaiśvānara shone upon the back of heaven; with his light he drives away the darkness.

sanskrit: hariṇasya patatriṇaḥ śīrṣṇo bheṣajam ābhṛtam | tan nīlavad vi lokavat tad u kṣetriyanāśanam ||
english: The remedy has been brought from the head of the flying deer — that which is as blue-tinged as it is bright-gleaming; and that indeed destroys the hereditary disease.

sanskrit: anvamaṃstānumatir anvaṃaṃsta vṛṣāyaveḥ | kīnāśā anvamaṃsata- -anu gāvo amaṃsata ||
english: Anumati approved; the bull's son approved. The ploughmen approved; the cows too approved.

sanskrit: namo astv āyāmibhyo nīvibhyo hṛdayāya ca | namaḥ kṣetrasya pataye namaḥ kṣetrasya patnyai ||
english: Reverence to the stretching ones, to the fastened garment-cords, and to the heart. Reverence to the lord of the field; reverence to the lady of the field.

sanskrit: ut te hārdiṃ śocayāmi hastenābhimarīmṛśat | keśin vṛṣaṇyayā tava muṣkau mūrdhā na śuṣyatām ||
english: I inflame thine inmost heart, touching it over with the hand. O long-haired one, by thy bull-lust let thy testicles not wither like a head.

sanskrit: agniṣ ṭvā tapatu sūryas tvā tapatu vātas tvā yuṅktāṃ marutaś ca yuñjatām | mṛgān marīcīr apy etu te manaḥ ||
english: Let Agni heat thee; let the Sun heat thee; let the Wind yoke thee and the Maruts yoke thee. Let thy mind go after the wild deer, after the mirages.

sanskrit: ut tvā hanmi nipadanād ut tvā hanmi gṛhebhyaḥ | mā spṛkṣathā niṣadanāya sādhava ut tiṣṭha prehi sabhām ||
english: I rouse thee up from languishing; I rouse thee up from the house. Do not touch upon sitting idle, O good one; stand up, go forward to the assembly.

sanskrit: ut tuda śimidāvaty atho ulkāvatīṃ kuru | patye ca śvaśurāya ca ||
english: Stir up the one who is slow to be stirred, and make her one who carries the torch, for her husband and for her father-in-law.

sanskrit: vibarhaṃ harāṃsayo rasaṃ jñānam ati bhruvoḥ | sākam ṛṣe vi nāśaya ||
english: O Harāṃsayu, destroy utterly together, O seer, the vital essence and the knowledge that flow over the eyebrows.

sanskrit: sākaṃ vātasya dhrājyā sākaṃ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ | sākaṃ sūryeṇodyatā sapatnīṃ nāśayāmasi ||
english: Together with the rushing of the wind, together with the rays of the Sun, together uplifted with the Sun, we destroy the rival wife.

sanskrit: dīrghajihvā bṛhadvāco yābhir ārdrāṇi vāsāṃsi | gāvo ghṛtasya mātaro divi bheṣajam akrata ||
english: The long-tongued, loud-voiced ones by whom wet garments arise — the cows, mothers of ghee, have made a remedy in heaven.

sanskrit: arjunīnām apacitāṃ kṛṣṇā māteti susrava | muner devasya mūlena sarvāś chinadmi tā aham ||
english: The black one, mother by name, has flowed forth — the outgrowth of the bright ones. With the root of the divine sage I cut all those away.

sanskrit: chinadmy āsāṃ prathamāṃ chinadmy uta madhyamām | atho jaghanyām āsām ā chinadmi stukām iva ||
english: I cut away the first of them; I cut away the middle one as well; and then I cut away the last of them entirely, like a tuft of hair.

sanskrit: apehi manasas pate kim aśastāni śaṃsasi | parehi na tvā kāmaye vṛkṣān vanāni saṃ cara ||
english: Go away, O lord of the mind! Why dost thou proclaim ill-omened things? Depart — I desire thee not; roam among trees and forests.

sanskrit: avaśasā niḥśasā yat parāśasā- -upārima yaj jāgrato yat svapantaḥ | agnir viśvāny apa duṣkṛtāny ajuṣṭāny āre asmad dadhātu ||
english: What we have incurred through ill speech, through base speech, through hostile speech — what while waking, what while sleeping — may Agni place all misdeeds and all that is displeasing far away from us.

sanskrit: yad indra brahmaṇaspata uta mṛṣā carāmasi | pracetā na āṅgiraso dviṣatas pātu tebhyaḥ ||
english: Whatever falsehood we practice, O Indra, O Brahmaṇaspati — may Pracetas the Āṅgirasa guard us from those who hate us.

sanskrit: eha mām uttaraṃ kṛdhi sahasva pṛtanāyataḥ | vy asmat kṛtyā vy asmac chapathām̐ aja ||
english: Here make me supreme; overpower the one who makes battle against me. Drive away the sorcery from us; drive away the curses from us.

sanskrit: yo no dudhūrṣān manasā yaś ca pāpena nobhyamāt | ākūtiṃ tasya devā hṛdaś cittāni vi ṣyata ||
english: He who would shake us with his mind, and he who has pressed upon us with evil — the intention of that one, O gods, release the heart's thoughts.

sanskrit: aśva iva dhuri duryogaḥ pratīhāya vahe daśa | kṛtvānaṃ brahmaṇaspate daṃṣṭrābhyām abhi saṃ jahi ||
english: Like a horse at the pole, difficult to yoke, I carry ten as a counter-draught. O Brahmaṇaspati, smite the sorcerer with both thy tusks.

sanskrit: yo 'nyā adhi prājāyathā mūrdhno 'dhy ud avardhatāḥ | tvaṃ sapatnacātano bhrātṛvyām̐ ava dhūnuṣva ||
english: Thou who art born above others, who hast grown up above the crown of the head — O rival-banisher, shake down the adversaries.

sanskrit: bahur ayaṃ saṃgaruṣṭo nyakto bhūmyām adhi | tenāham asya kartsyāmi yathā sthāmā gamiṣyati ||
english: This one is mighty, enraged in conflict, pressed down upon the earth. With that I shall bring him to naught so that he shall go to the place of standing still.

sanskrit: sthāmāgan bṛhad akṣatraḥ sthāmantākṣṇiṇo 'va syati | antaṣṭhānasya yo rājā sa utthāma gamiṣyati ||
english: He has come to a standstill, the great one without a domain; the one with cramped limbs falls at the standstill. Whoever is king of that inner standing-place — he shall go to the highest standing.

sanskrit: agamad rājā sadanam agamat sūryo divam | udayan vṛtrahan plīhā aṅgarājo avīrahā ||
english: The king has gone to his abode; the Sun has gone to the sky. Rising, O Vṛtra-slayer, the spleen — the king of limbs, the slayer of men — has gone.

sanskrit: yathā panthāṃ kavāpatho apyeti mahāpatham | evā tvaṃ plīhan naḥ plīhi yato 'sy abhyāgataḥ ||
english: As a bypath merges into the great road, so do thou, O spleen, return to us whence thou hast come attacking.

sanskrit: indreṇa dattaṃ balam āsurābhyāṃ śitaṅgaitac chālvatāyai ca tubhyam | tau nudethāṃ kaṇvā aśivā ajuṣṭā adhā gṛhāṇāṃ gṛhapā tvam eṣām ||
english: The strength given by Indra — this from the Āsuras, Śitaṅga and from Śālvata too — to thee: let those two drive away the evil, unpleasing Kaṇvas; then be thou the house-lord of these houses.

sanskrit: tvam agne gṛhapatir gṛhāṇāṃ tvaṃ prajānāṃ janitāsi dātā | tvaṃ nudasva kaṇvā aśivā ajuṣṭā sadānvā nirataḥ seda pāpīḥ ||
english: Thou, O Agni, art the house-lord of the houses; thou art the begetter and giver of offspring. Do thou thrust away the evil, unpleasing Kaṇvas, always repelled, driven out hence, these sinful ones.

sanskrit: carmābhyaḥ krūram ānahya hariṇasya bhiyaṃ kṛdhi | mṛgām̐ anu pra pātaya marīcīr anu nāśaya ||
english: Having bound the cruel thing with hides, cause the fear of the deer. Drive the wild animals forward; destroy the mirages.

sanskrit: yady asy apsarāvīr yadi tvā rakṣo agrabhīt | tasmā apaplavaṃ havir manasā juhomi te ||
english: If thou art afflicted by Apsaras, if a demon has seized thee — for that I pour for thee an apaplava oblation with my mind.
